title: crystal API
description: What crystal's CLI and its daemon say to each other over the daemon's socket: one JSON object a line, a request, then the response to it. An `attach` goes on in bytes, not JSON: the session's output from the daemon, and from the client frames of keys and sizes. `schemas` names each message, and `$defs` holds the types they're made of.

request.title: what a client sends the daemon
request.description: A request: one JSON object on a line, its kind in `type`, beside the version of the crystal that sent it. The daemon answers it with one response, on a line of its own, and hangs up, but for a `subscribe`, an `attach` and a `take_layout_orders`, which go on after it.

version.description: The version of the crystal that sent it, as `crystal --version` prints it. The daemon refuses a request from a crystal of another version than its own, or one that doesn't say, but for a `shutdown` and a `handover`, which every daemon takes whatever the version.

response.title: what the daemon answers
response.description: A response: one JSON object on a line, its kind in `type`. An `error` says why the request couldn't be carried out, and a `timed_out` that a wait gave up.

event.title: what a subscription streams
event.description: An event: one JSON object on a line, its kind in `event`, as a `subscribe` streams them after its `subscribed`, `crystal events --json` prints them and plugins' hooks are given them. Only the fields its kind carries are there.

layout_order.title: what the daemon hands a TUI taking layout orders
layout_order.description: A layout order: after a `take_layout_orders` is answered `done`, the daemon writes the TUI each command to carry out on a line, numbered for its answer.

layout_report.title: what that TUI tells the daemon
layout_report.description: A layout report: what a TUI taking layout orders writes back, a line at a time: that it was used, that its terminal gained or lost the focus, and each order's answer.

snapshot.title: what `crystal api snapshot` prints
snapshot.description: A snapshot: everything a client that keeps its own picture of crystal starts from, with the latest event's `seq` to follow on from.

oneOf.description: Working on a turn.
Stopped until the user answers it, say a permission prompt.
Finished its turn, and nobody has looked at it since.
Finished its turn, and it has been seen.

Activity.description: What the agent in a session is doing.

oneOf.description: The agent is up and waiting for its first prompt.
A tool call finished, so the agent is back to work, say after the user allowed it.
The agent is asking the user something: a permission, a question.
The agent has sat at its prompt for a while.
The agent started a subagent, which says nothing about what the agent itself is doing.
One of its subagents finished. The agent's turn goes on.
The agent named the conversation it's in, which says nothing about what it's doing: a hook that runs at no point of a turn crystal can tell, or one whose agent says too little to read its turns by.

AgentEvent.description: What an agent's hooks report, in terms that fit any agent. The daemon works out the session's `Activity` from these.

oneOf.description: It's doing `state`, which takes the session's status over from crystal's own reading of it. `None` for the agent keeps the name it gave before; `resume`, the command that picks its session up again.
Only the command that picks its session up again, from an agent that holds the session.
It lets go of the session: crystal reads what the session does for itself again, and forgets the agent's name and command.

AgentReport.description: What an agent says about itself with `crystal report`.

oneOf.description: Yes, this once.
Yes, and a rule for calls like it, so they're not asked about again.

Answer.description: An answer to the permission a background task asks for.

id.description: The id it had, which it keeps in the archive.

worktree.description: The worktree it ran in, as it was then.

archived.description: When it was archived, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

ArchivedSession.description: A session kept in the archive: what it takes to start it again, where it ran, and when it was archived.

name.description: The copy's name, which is the file's own unless two had one name.

Artifact.description: A file kept with a task as it closed: copied out of its worktree into crystal's state directory, so it outlives the worktree.

oneOf.description: A file `crystal done --artifact` named.
The worktree's handoff file as it was when the task closed.

Asking.description: A permission a background task's Claude asks for: the tool, and what it's asked to do with it, like `Bash` and `cargo test`.

project.description: The project's name, as the sidebar shows it.

path.description: The project's main worktree, or the directory itself outside git.

tasks.description: The project's tasks started for an item, open, waiting or closed, with tasks on: each item's history.

Backlog.description: One project's backlog: things to do later.

number.description: Its number in the project's backlog, which never changes: #1, #2…

text.description: One line on what's to do.

body.description: More on it, when one line isn't enough: empty, or a few lines.

created.description: When it was put on the backlog, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

closed.description: When it was done, while it is.

ContextUse.description: How full a conversation's context is: the tokens the model was given for its last message, of the most its model takes.

transcript.description: The file the agent keeps the conversation in.

prompted.description: Whether the agent has worked on a turn in it, for a conversation whose hooks don't say where it's kept.

Conversation.description: An agent's conversation, as its hooks name it: what it takes to pick the conversation up again after a restart.

DaemonAbout.description: The daemon, handed over to another crystal: the version it runs now, and how many sessions carried on through it. The version it ran before is the event's `from`. Or restarted cold: how many sessions it started again, and those that couldn't start, by name.

made_lessons.description: How many of the notes it was shown it made lessons.

DistillAbout.description: A pass of the distiller over what a session did: how many entries it added to the project's memory, found there already and turned down, how many of those gone stale it kept, reworded or forgot, and what it cost; or why it failed.

added.description: The ids of the entries it added.

again.description: The ids of the entries the project had already, seen again.

forgotten.description: How many it found that the user had forgotten.

kept.description: The ids of the stale entries it said still hold, anchored again.

reworded.description: The ids of the stale entries it reworded.

forgot.description: The ids of the stale entries it said no longer hold, forgotten.

rejected.description: The entries the model gave that didn't pass, each with why.

cost_usd.description: What the pass cost, in US dollars, as Claude counts it.

made_lessons.description: The ids of the notes it was shown that it made lessons.

on_disk.description: How much of the models is on disk, in bytes, downloaded or on its way, and how much they are in all.

loaded.description: Whether the daemon has them loaded.

preparing.description: What the daemon is doing to get them ready, while it does.

failed.description: Why getting them ready last failed.

entries.description: How many entries every project has, and how many of them have their vector from the model searches use now.

embedder.description: What searches use, as its vectors are kept under: `MODEL`, or Gemini's model at its size.

gemini.description: How Gemini stands, while searches use it.

EmbeddingStatus.description: How the models stand, as the settings view shows them.

seq.description: Its place in the log: 1 for the first event, and one more for each after it. The daemon gives it as it writes the event down.

at.description: When it happened, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

project.description: The project it's about: its main worktree, or the directory itself outside git.

from.description: What it was before: a renamed session's old name, what its agent was doing before it changed, or the agent that let go of it; a renamed tab's old name, the number a tab had before it moved or of the tab in front before, the number of the tab a session moved from, or the session or project the user was on before; the ids of the entries of memory merged into one.

artifact.description: A file kept with a task as it closed.

subagent.description: The subagent a session's agent started, or that finished.

distill.description: What the distiller made of what a session did, or why it couldn't.

file.description: The file it's about: the instructions file an entry of memory was written into.

tab.description: The tab it's about, as `crystal layout --json` has it: as it is now, or as it was, closed; for a session focused or moved, the tab it's in.

Event.description: Something that happened. Only the fields its kind carries are there.

EventKind.description: What happened. A kind can be added, but never renamed or taken away.

Extent.description: A popup's width or height: so many cells, or a share of the screen.

kinds.description: Names or patterns, the way a plugin's `on` takes them: `session.waiting`, `task.*`, `*`. None takes every kind.

session.description: Only those about the session with this name or id.

project.description: Only those about the project whose main worktree this is.

task.description: Only those about the task with this number: the task itself, and its session while it works on it.

Filter.description: Which events a reader wants: every one, but for what it says.

name.description: What it's run by: `crystal flow run <name>`. Its runs and their sessions are named after it, so it can't have spaces.

description.description: A line on what it's for, shown in the new-session panel.

step.description: The steps, in the order they run: `[[flow.step]]` tables.

flow.description: The flow it runs, by its name in the config file.

state.description: How the step, or the whole run, stands: `running`, `waiting`, `done` or `failed`; for a gate answered, `approved` or `sent back`.

said.description: The first line of a step's answer or of why it failed, or the notes a gate was sent back with.

cost_usd.description: What a step's run cost, or once the run ends, all of it, in US dollars.

FlowAbout.description: A flow run, and the step an event is about.

name.description: The flow's name and a number: `ship-1`, `ship-2`…

flow.description: The flow as it was when the run started, so that changing the config file doesn't change a run halfway.

profiles.description: The profiles its steps run with, as they were then too.

goal.description: What the user asked for: `{goal}` in each step's prompt.

cwd.description: The directory it was started in.

worktree.description: The worktree it made for its steps, once a step has wanted one.

round.description: 1 to start with, and one more each time the flow is sent back.

feedback.description: What the last send back said: `{feedback}` in each step's prompt from then on.

steps.description: How each of the flow's steps stands, in the same order.

started.description: When it started, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

name.description: What the step is called, in its flow and in its session's name.

profile.description: The `[[profile]]` it runs with, for its agent, model, mode, arguments, instructions and prompt. Left out, Claude Code as it's set up.

agent.description: The agent it runs, one crystal knows (`claude`, `codex`, …), in place of its profile's: see `Step::profile_in`.

model.description: The model, in place of its profile's.

effort.description: How hard it thinks, Claude Code's `--effort`, in place of its profile's.

mode.description: How it asks before acting, in place of its profile's.

background.description: Whether it runs in the background, as `claude -p`. Left out, a step on Claude Code does, and one on any other agent runs in a terminal; `false` runs Claude Code in a terminal too. Only Claude Code runs in the background.

prompt.description: What it's asked, with `{goal}` and the rest filled in: see `crate::flow_run::FlowRun::prompt_for`.

accept.description: What has to hold before it's done: its task's acceptance criteria, which its agent is told under its prompt.

placement.description: Where it runs. Left out, where the step before it ran, or for the first step, where the run started.

gate.description: Stop after this step until the user goes on, or sends it back.

back_to.description: The step that sending the flow back from this one's gate runs again, like `implement` for a review. Left out, this step itself.

max_rounds.description: On a gate: how many rounds the flow may take through it, 1 to `MAX_ROUNDS`; in the last, it can't be sent back. Left out, `MAX_ROUNDS`.

FlowStep.description: One step of a flow: a task.

Forge.description: The forges crystal speaks to, each through its own CLI.

ForgeLink.description: A pull request or an issue a task is about: which forge it's on, its number, title and address, and for a pull request, the branch its worktree is on.

oneOf.description: Everything it names is in the code still; or naming nothing to look for, none of its files has changed since it was said, or it has none.
Some of what it names is gone from the code; or naming nothing to look for, some of its files have changed since: it may hold only in part.
Everything it names is gone from the code; or naming nothing to look for, every one of its files is gone: it may no longer hold at all.

Freshness.description: Whether an entry still holds, by what it names, or with nothing to look for, the files it's about. The fresher sorts first.

oneOf.description: A coding agent crystal knows: its program, like `claude`, and what it's called, like `Claude Code`.
Any other program, by its name.
A task: Claude Code run without a terminal.

Front.description: What's in front in a session's terminal: the program its keys go to.

model.description: The model and its size, as each vector is kept under: `gemini-embedding-2@768`.

key.description: Where the key is read from, or `None` with none found.

key_shared.description: Whether the key's file can be read by others than its owner.

failed.description: Why the key can't be had, or why the last request failed, while none has worked since; and how many seconds ago it failed.

tokens.description: How many tokens Google has counted since the process started.

GeminiStatus.description: How the Gemini API stands for memory, as the daemon says it does.

HandoffAbout.description: A note added to a worktree's handoff file.

name.description: Its program's name, as the system keeps it: cut to 15 bytes.

HelperUsage.description: What a process the daemon runs that isn't a session's takes, with every process under it: the distiller's `claude -p`, git, a plugin's hook.

InProgress.description: What git is in the middle of in a worktree: a merge, a rebase, a cherry-pick or a revert that stopped, on conflicts say, and waits to be finished or aborted. Nothing should cut through it: no switch of branch, and no task closed done.

oneOf.description: As the new-session panel is set.
In a terminal, what it's asked only its first prompt: a session, not a task, with nothing to close.
In a terminal, as a task, which `crystal done` closes.
As a background task, `claude -p`, for Claude Code; another agent starts as a task in a terminal.

Launch.description: How a profile's agent is meant to start.

presence.description: Whether the user is at crystal, by what every TUI's terminal says of its focus: the daemon says, as a TUI knows only its own.

Layout.description: A TUI's tabs and their panes.

oneOf.description: Nothing: the layout as it is.
Make a tab after the others, called `name` if it's given, and bring it to the front, where sessions started from then on go.
Bring a tab to the front: by its number, from 1, or its name.
Name a tab; an empty name takes it back to its number.
Close a tab, the one in front unless `tab` says. One that holds sessions closes only with `kill`, which kills them with it.
Move a session to another tab.
Move a tab to `position`, from 1, the others making room.
Show `session` in a pane of its own, split off `way` from the pane of `beside`, which keeps `ratio` of the room.
Select a session, bringing its tab to the front, and hand its pane the keyboard; with `raise`, bring the TUI's terminal to the front too, as a click on a notification does.
The same for the session in the pane `toward` from the pane of the session it's about.
Move a border of a session's pane `cells` columns or rows `toward`, or as far as a key in resize mode does when it's `None`.
Swap a session's pane with the pane `toward` from it, the splits and their ratios left as they are.
The same with the pane of `with`, in the same tab.
Give a session's pane's side of the split nearest above it, or the nearest `way` when that's given, `share` of the split's room.
Close a session's pane of its own: its split closes, or its float is put back.
Zoom a session's pane over its tab, selecting it there, or with `on` false, put the tab's panes back.
Even out the panes of the tab the command was run in, or else the one in front.
Float a session over its tab's panes, or with `on` false, put the tab's float back among them.

Show `session`, the pane of the plugin called `plugin`, over the panes with the keyboard, under `title`, or in a popup that size, until its program ends or the user closes it, which kills it. Only a TUI can.

Show `files`, text files by their absolute paths, in a view of their own over the tabs, each by its path from `dir`, the worktree they were opened in, where an editor opening one starts: `crystal open`. Only a TUI can.
Give the TUI's terminal the title `text`, in place of the one the settings make, or with none, go back to that one.

Move a session in the sidebar's order by hand, among those beside it in its worktree; or, with `project`, the project with its main worktree there, among the projects. The order lasts across restarts.

Lay tabs out as `tabs` has them, their numbers aside: each in place of the tab with its name, or after the others when it has none or there's no such tab; or with `replace`, in place of every tab, the sessions they don't hold joining the tab in front. The sessions they hold move to them, and one `current` comes to the front. The sessions are all there by now: `crystal layout apply` starts those that weren't (see `crate::layout_file`).

LayoutCommand.description: What a TUI is asked to do with its tabs and panes. A session named is one of the TUI's; one that isn't named is the session the command was run in, or else the one selected.

caller.description: The id of the session the command was run in, when it was run in one: the session it's about when it names none.

LayoutOrder.description: A command as a TUI gets it.

oneOf.description: The user did something in it, so orders go to it from now on.
Its terminal has gained the focus, or lost it.
What came of the order numbered `id`: the layout it came to, or why it couldn't be carried out.
What changed in its tabs and panes, for the daemon to tell whoever listens: see `crate::tui::layout_events`.

LayoutReport.description: What a TUI tells the daemon, a line at a time, once it takes orders.

id.description: Unlike its name, a session's id never changes: it's how a program tells which session it runs in, whatever the session is called now.

activity.description: `None` for a program that doesn't report what it's doing.

worktree.description: `None` when the session's directory isn't in a git repository.

changed.description: When the session last changed, in seconds since the Unix epoch: it started, its agent started or stopped doing something, or its program ended. 0 from a daemon that doesn't say.

front.description: What's in front in the session's terminal, which can change as it runs: a shell can have an agent in front, and the shell back. `None` until it's been looked at, and from a daemon that doesn't say.

task.description: What the session's agent was asked to do, when it was, and how that went.

asking.description: The permission a background task is waiting on the user for.

reporter.description: The agent that says what it's doing itself, with `crystal report`, while it holds the session.

subagents.description: How many subagents its agent has running, as its hooks say.

model.description: The model its agent runs on, as it said with `crystal report --model`, or else as its command, its hooks or its transcript have it, following a switch like Claude Code's `/model`.

line.description: The line an agent or a script put on its row with `crystal report --line`, until it's taken off or its time is up; or, held working while work of its own runs, what that is.

row.description: The rest of what `crystal report` put on its row: a title, the agent it says is in front, labels for its statuses and tokens.

bell.description: Its program rang the terminal's bell while nobody was watching, and nobody has looked at it since.

unseen_copies.description: How many times its program asked its terminal to copy something while nobody was watching, since the daemon started: crystal put none of them on the clipboard. A TUI says so as the count goes up.

stopped_idle.description: crystal stopped it after its agent sat idle for as long as the settings allow: it starts again in its conversation.

context.description: How full a background task's conversation is, once Claude has said.

output_waits.description: How many `crystal wait --output` the daemon is looking at its screen for: a script can tell its wait has reached the daemon.

ListedSession.description: A session as `ls --json` lists it: what the daemon knows, and the word its STATE column shows.

bytes.description: Its memory, in bytes: 0 when it can't say.

cores.description: Its cores, those online: 0 when it can't say.

id.description: Counts up from 1 in each project, so it's short enough to type.

files.description: The files it's about, from the top of the project.

created.description: When it was added, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

seen.description: How many times it has been said: once, then once more each time someone says the same again.

last_seen.description: When it was last said, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

anchors.description: The SHA-256 of each of its files that was there when it was last said, by file, to tell whether they've changed since.

checkout.description: The worktree its files were hashed in; the project's main worktree when it's `None`.

names.description: What its text names that was in the code when it was last said: the identifiers, paths, commands and flags in it, to tell whether they're still there.

used.description: When an agent last read it in full, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

counted_from.description: When its time to expire counts from, when that's later than when it was last said: when crystal started telling whether an entry is found again, for one from before then, or when it was made a note.

oneOf.description: A choice made, and why.
Something that catches people out.
A command that does something useful here.
How a task turned out, as an earlier crystal kept it as each task closed: found by a search, never shown at launch, and not something to add any more.

MemoryKind.description: What sort of thing an entry is.

gone.description: What it names that's gone from the code since it was said; or, naming nothing to look for, the files it's about that are gone.

MemoryListed.description: An entry, with whether it still holds.

MemoryMerge.description: Entries of a project that say the same thing, as `crystal memory dedupe` finds them: the one kept, and those that go into it, each as alike to it as it is.

checkout.description: The worktree its files are in, from its top; the project's main worktree when it's `None`.

MemoryNew.description: An entry about to be added.

oneOf.description: A session, by its name when it added the entry.
A task, by its name, as it ended.
The distiller, from what the task of this name did.

MemoryTwin.description: An entry said before, and how alike it is to another, which says the same thing: by the model's vectors, from -1 to 1, and by the reranker, reading the other as the query, when it was asked.

from.description: The session that sent it, by name, when another session did; `None` from the user, or a script.

line.description: The first line of what it says, after the line saying who sent it.

MessageAbout.description: A message a session was sent with `crystal send`, or from the TUI.

line.description: A short line under its row; empty takes it off.

model.description: The model its agent runs on, in place of what crystal reads; empty gives that back.

title.description: What a row laid out with `title` says in place of the session's name; empty takes it off.

display_agent.description: What the row says is in front, in place of the agent crystal reads; empty gives that back.

state_labels.description: What a row laid out with `state` says for a status, by the status's word (`waiting`, `working`, `done`, `idle`, …); an empty one takes that status's off.

tokens.description: The values of tokens a row laid out with `$name` shows, by their names; an empty one takes that token off. Those not named stay as they were.

ttl_secs.description: How long what this says stays, in seconds, unless it's said again: until it's replaced, with none.

seq.description: The report's number from `source`: one numbered no higher than the last that source sent came late, and is passed over.

Metadata.description: What `crystal report --line`, `--model`, `--title`, `--display-agent`, `--state-label` and `--token` put on a session's row, or `crystal project report --token` on a project's.

branch.description: The branch it's on, which the agent is told.

MovedTo.description: The worktree a session moves into: see `crystal worktree move`.

done.description: Whether it's done already: ticked off as it's put there.

NewItem.description: An item to put on the backlog, as `crystal backlog import` read it.

name.description: `None` names the session for its task, or else after its program until its first prompt names it.

env.description: The client's environment, which the program starts from.

task.description: What the agent is asked to do, which makes the session a task. It's in `command` already, as the agent's first prompt; this says which part of the command it is.

backlog.description: The backlog item the task is for, which closing it done ticks.

accept.description: Its acceptance criteria, each one a line, which its agent is told under its goal.

pull_request.description: The pull request it works on, in whose worktree it runs.

agent_names.description: Whether the session's agent may name it, in place of the name crystal gives it, when the settings say so: for a client that doesn't hold on to that name, like the TUI, which follows a rename. A script that was told the name may use it later.

NewSession.description: What a task carries beside its goal: what has to hold before it's done, and the pull request and the issue it's about, on its project's forge.

name.description: `None` names the task for its prompt, or else "task", with a number added if that's taken.

env.description: The client's environment, which Claude starts from.

backlog.description: The backlog item the task is for, which closing it done ticks.

accept.description: Its acceptance criteria, each one a line, which its agent is told under its goal.

pull_request.description: The pull request it works on, in whose worktree it runs.

NewTask.description: What a task carries beside its goal: what has to hold before it's done, and the pull request and the issue it's about, on its project's forge.

oneOf.description: The one for an agent that's done.
The one for an agent asking the user something.

closed.description: When it was closed, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

TaskOutcome.description: How a task went, once it's closed.

session.description: The session it ran in, under the name it had then. Empty for a task that hasn't started.

pending.description: Made with `--no-launch`, and not started yet.

artifacts.description: The files kept with it as it closed.

accept.description: Its acceptance criteria, each one a line, which its agent is told under its goal.

pull_request.description: The pull request it works on, in whose worktree it runs.

TaskRecord.description: A task as `crystal tasks` lists it: one still open in a session, one waiting to start, or one closed, from its project's history.

text.description: What Claude said at the end of its last run, or what went wrong.

cost_usd.description: What the task has cost so far, in US dollars, as Claude counts it.

runs.description: How many times Claude has run for it: its prompt, then each follow-up.

TaskResult.description: What `crystal result` answers with: a task's last answer, and what the task has come to so far.

TaskSpec.description: What a task is asked to do: the prompt it starts with, and arguments for each `claude -p` it runs, like `--permission-mode acceptEdits`.

oneOf.description: An agent in a terminal: this command, with the goal in it as the agent's first prompt.
In the background, `claude -p` with these arguments.
Made to start later, with `--no-launch`: nothing works on it yet.
Its session is working on it.
Its agent's turn ended with it still open: it's asking the user something.
The user cancelled it, or killed its session while it was open.

session.description: The session it ran in, under the name it had then. Empty for a task that hasn't started.

pending.description: Made with `--no-launch`, and not started yet.

artifacts.description: The files kept with it as it closed.

accept.description: Its acceptance criteria, each one a line, which its agent is told under its goal.

pull_request.description: The pull request it works on, in whose worktree it runs.

session_state.description: How its session stands, while the session is still there.

asking.description: The permission a background task is waiting on the user for.

cost_usd.description: What a background task has cost so far, in US dollars.

context.description: How full a background task's conversation is, once Claude has said.

TaskView.description: A task as the CLI shows it: what's kept of it, how it stands, and, while a session works on it, what that session is doing.

oneOf.description: A session split off, or with `selection`, the pane that follows the selection, and the session it shows, if any.
The first side has `ratio` of the room, the second the rest.

Tile.description: A tab's panes: a pane, or a split of its room in two.

ToolUse.description: A tool a background task's Claude used: its name, and the gist of what it was given, like the command it ran.

why_not.description: Why it didn't match: the first thing it wanted that wasn't there.

seen.description: The start of the text it looked at.

TriedRule.description: A rule as it was tried on a screen.

oneOf.description: Once, this many seconds on.
Again and again, for as long as it runs.

Wakeup.description: Work an agent scheduled to wake it later, as its hooks say: Claude Code's `ScheduleWakeup`, which a `/loop` paces itself with, and `CronCreate`. An agent stopped meanwhile would never wake.

command.description: Its command, with no first prompt: Claude Code's.

env.description: The client's environment, which the program starts from.

task.description: Whether the session that takes it over is a task, with tasks on: the agent is told of closing it as it starts.

WarmAgent.description: What a warm agent is started as: what a new session that takes it over is started as, but for its first prompt, which is typed into it then.

project.description: The project's name: the name of its main worktree's directory.

project_path.description: The main worktree's directory, which tells projects apart.

main.description: Whether this is the repository's main worktree, rather than one linked to it with `git worktree add`.

branch.description: The branch checked out, or `None` when HEAD is detached. In the middle of a rebase, where git detaches HEAD until it's through, the branch being rebased.

in_progress.description: What git is in the middle of here, if anything, which leaves the worktree as it is until it's finished or aborted.

Worktree.description: The git worktree a session runs in, and the project it belongs to.

project.description: Its project's main worktree. A removed worktree's directory is gone, so git can't say which project it was in, unless crystal removed it.

why.description: Why the hook run on it failed, for `worktree.hook_failed`.

WorktreeAbout.description: A worktree crystal made or removed.
